title: Abell S1063 galaxy cluster
caption: The galaxy cluster Abell S1063, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: Abell S1063 · constellation Grus · about 4 billion light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, V. Kokorev (University of Texas at Austin), A. Pagan (STScI)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Webb press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A bright-white elliptical galaxy sits at the center of this field, the core of the galaxy cluster Abell S1063. Around it curl short red arcs, the images of far more distant galaxies, magnified and warped. A couple of foreground stars shine large and bright, each with Webb's signature eight-point spikes.

Galaxy clusters are among the most massive objects in the Universe, and their gravity bends light passing near them, an effect called gravitational lensing. Webb was observing this cluster for a different purpose when, by luck, it also caught a little red dot later named GLIMPSE-17775.

GLIMPSE-17775 belongs to a class of objects that astronomers call little red dots. Lensing, combined with 30 hours of Webb observing time, let scientists record the deepest spectrum yet of one of them. It gave the strongest evidence so far for a hot, dense cocoon of gas known as a "black hole star".
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.19 x 2.19 arcminutes) and distance (4 billion light years), the frame spans roughly 2.5 million × 2.5 million light-years. Its light set out about 4,000 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image comes from Webb's NIRCam. The shortest wavelengths, from 900 nm to 1.5 micrometers, are shown in blue, those around 2.0 to 2.77 micrometers in green, and the longest, 3.56 to 4.44 micrometers, in red.
understand.eye: Almost all of this light is infrared, invisible to the eye, so the colors are a translation of wavelengths we cannot see.

explore: A spectrum spreads an object's light out by wavelength, revealing what it is made of and how it behaves. Getting a deep one of such a faint object depends on both long observing time and the natural magnification that the cluster provides.
alt: A field of galaxies on black with a bright-white elliptical galaxy at the center, short curved red arcs around it, and a couple of bright foreground stars with eight-point spikes.
